Active cell: 2px border rgb(43,87,201) (ring token) and a 4px halo rgb(232,238,251) (primary-subtle); digits 24px/800; radius 12px. Invalid cell border rgb(180,35,24) (destructive). assumptions: The shadcn CLI added the cn package and a cn import from "cn", so the spec rule applied: manual installation, cn from @/lib/utils, no other package.
Disabled cells take the muted look through the container group and group-has-disabled: (a variant on the cells), because has-disabled: on the container cannot style its children; no opacity anywhere.
text-heading is the colour utility, so the 24px digits use text-(length:--text-heading); lib/utils.ts is untouched and no cn call gets text-label with text-heading.
The active cell takes a negative 1px margin so the thicker border does not make it 2px wider than its neighbours (flex-basis 0 counts borders); seen in Chromium at 320 before the fix.
The paste error stays until Verify (React Hook Form revalidates on submit), even if a valid paste follows, as for every other field error.

Existing assertions changed beyond the spec list: the locked state test (the help is now a region after the surface, not a bare line), typed-entry refusal tests (a typed letter and seven digits), echo checks rescoped as the spec says; the end-of-wait focus checks sit in dedicated tests because a user click on a disabled button moves focus to body, in jsdom and in browsers.
Not built, outside the spec: the mockup .surface card around the OTP form, the info notice for the neutral sentence, and the muted label of a disabled field (field.tsx is not in Touches).
useRateLimit takes the notice and submit refs from the screen, because the react-hooks/refs lint rejects reading a ref object that a hook returns.

Gateway: both images read the one template: the Dockerfile copies templates/ to /etc/nginx/templates/ (local) and copies templates/security-headers.conf.template into /etc/nginx/templates-aws/ (AWS); both nginx.conf templates include /etc/nginx/security-headers.conf. The two cases of AppOrigin_ContentSecurityPolicies_HoldBaseUriNone (AWS and local images) prove it by response.
Gateway: the new hash test is a file test, but it sits in GatewayTests (as the spec names) and so runs with that class's container fixture.

Gateway: PlatformTests ran on macOS under the stack lock, not in the Linux SDK container: GatewayTests drive the host Docker daemon, prior gateway builds ran them the same way, and the change touches no shell tooling; CI's ubuntu run is the Linux result.

Gateway: scripts/security-local.sh not run: no Terraform, Dockerfile or Compose file changed (an nginx header template only). floor-guard clean; secret-scan no leaks; dotnet build of PlatformTests 0 warnings; dotnet format style and whitespace --verify-no-changes clean.

Gateway security self-check: the header is loosened by exactly the human-decided D1 hash. A hash-source admits only an inline style element whose content hashes to it, so only an empty element; it does not cover style attributes (no unsafe-hashes) and adds no unsafe-inline or nonce. Rules inserted through the CSSOM are not governed by style-src, which is why input-otp works with an empty element, and script-src 'self' still blocks the script any CSSOM injection would need. The security agent reviews this against CSP Level 3 and AD-23.

input-otp slices a paste to six characters before it checks the pattern, so a paste with exactly 6 digits and other characters is accepted with the rest dropped ('481516a' and '481516\n' give 481516, as the fix list asks). A paste with more than 6 digits, whatever else it holds, is refused (decision 2026-11-08). A paste whose letters push its first six characters off the digits ('48151a') is still dropped whole by the library with no error, as the spec's Inputs table says.

A refused paste while the summary from an earlier failed Verify is showing leaves that summary in place and does not move focus; the field error and the announcement are the same words. '481-5167' (7 digits with a hyphen) is now refused as 7 digits.
